narrative.summary: The OIC's AI texts recorded here come from two of its organs: the Independent Permanent Human Rights Commission's Jeddah Declaration on guiding principles for AI governance (2024) and the International Islamic Fiqh Academy's resolution on artificial intelligence (2025). Both are non-binding.

instruments.official_title: Jeddah Declaration on the Guiding Principles of Artificial Intelligence Governance and Human Rights Protection
instruments.english_title: Jeddah Declaration on the Guiding Principles of Artificial Intelligence Governance and Human Rights Protection
instruments.issuing_authority: OIC Independent Permanent Human Rights Commission (IPHRC), 23rd Regular Session
instruments.publisher_name: OIC Independent Permanent Human Rights Commission (IPHRC), 23rd Regular Session
instruments.summary: Declaration of the OIC's human rights commission setting guiding principles for AI governance and human rights. It recommends that OIC Member States build political support for laws and regulatory measures addressing AI's human rights impacts, take part in Global Digital Compact negotiations, invest in AI literacy, consider independent national bodies to audit AI systems and provide redress, support human rights impact assessments, protect women, children and persons with disabilities, and share AI governance expertise; it also suggests an OIC centre for digital technology cooperation.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the OIC Independent Permanent Human Rights Commission at its 23rd Regular Session in Jeddah on 4 July 2024. Its recommendations are addressed to OIC Member States and the OIC General Secretariat.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read on the IPHRC official site. Date line: 'Issued in the city of Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, on 28/12/1445, corresponding to 4th July 2024.' IPHRC members are independent experts elected by the CFM, so this is an organ text, not a state-adopted declaration; reviewer may prefer to treat it as a lead. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, date 4 July 2024 (28/12/1445 H), Jeddah, 23rd Regular Session of the OIC-IPHRC and all summary recommendations confirmed on oic-iphrc.org PDF.; current_status: the document does not describe the IPHRC as an 'advisory expert organ' and does not say its recommendations are not binding.; legal_status: the document is self-titled a Declaration of an OIC organ; 'declaration' fits better than 'nonbinding_guidance'.

instruments.official_title: Resolution No. 258 (3/26): Artificial Intelligence: Its Rulings, Guidelines, and Ethics
instruments.english_title: International Islamic Fiqh Academy Resolution No. 258 (3/26) on Artificial Intelligence: Its Rulings, Guidelines, and Ethics
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC, 26th session
instruments.publisher_name: Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC, 26th session
instruments.summary: Jurisprudential resolution on AI. It holds that developing and using AI is permissible subject to six conditions: lawful purpose, use, funding and outcomes; bringing benefit and preventing harm; not insulting beliefs, religions or religious symbols; protecting information and public and private rights and freedoms; not threatening individual, societal or national security; and upholding honesty, documentation and transparency. It recommends further study of whether AI can be given legal personality and specialised symposiums on AI ethics.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC at its 26th session in Doha, State of Qatar (4–8 May 2025); published on the Academy's site on 20 November 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read on the IIFA official site. Session printed as Doha, Dhul-Qi'dah 1446H (4–8 May 2025); the page also carries a post date of 20 November 2025. Month of adoption used. Arabic original presumably on iifa-aifi.org/ar (not opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: Resolution No. 258 (3/26), title, 26th session in Doha, Qatar (Dhul-Qi'dah 1446H, 4-8 May 2025), issuer 'Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation', six conditions and two recommendations confirmed on iifa-aifi.org (page dated 20 November 2025).; current_status: the page does not call the IIFA a 'subsidiary organ' of the OIC nor say the text is not binding on states.
